newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt up as yield spreads tighten.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt up as yield spreads tighten.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices outperformed U.S. Treasuries for the second straight day, causing yield spreads on Brady bonds of Argentina, Brazil and Mexico to narrow five to 10 basis points, market sources said.

"Our market is still holding in very nicely. I see spread tightening in Argentina, Brazil and Mexico all in the order of five to 10 basis points," said Dan Peirce, chief emerging market strategist at BankBoston.
At 1635 EST/2135 GMT, Argentine FRBs were 3/8 firmer at 89-1/8 bid, Brazilian "C" bonds were 5/8 stronger at 76-1/4 and Mexican pars were 1/2 firmer at 74-1/2 bid.
Sources attributed most of the gains in the emerging debt market to excess liquidity and some cross over buying.
In Brazil, market sources said the country's Brady prices have already factored in passage of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's reelection amendment which would allow him to serve a second term.
Brazil's Chamber of Deputies began voting on the bill and a decision was expected late Tuesday evening.
Although market participants were optimistic about Cardoso's re-election amendement, one market source said the real problem for Brazil could be a ballooning of the country's internal debt.
"The real struggle for Brazil is if their internal debt starts to blow up and the fiscal sitution starts to look a bit dicey," the source said.
Among Eastern European assets, sources said Bulgaria was the exception in the market as political uncertainty continued to hurt the country's debt instruments.

Even though the Bulgarian government made a $135.1 million coupon payment on its Brady bonds earlier today, the news failed to bolster the price of the bonds because of the country's political situation.

"The coupon payment was made, so my view is that they have some time on their hands until the next Brady payment and hopefully they will do the right thing but it's just not clear how quickly progress will be," he said.
Bulgarian IABs were 1-1/8 lower at 48-5/8 bid and the country's FLRBs were one percentage point weaker at 35-1/2 bid.
